title: Keeping the crew in touch when the level splits you
target: How to use the walkie-talkie, the chat box and the map in R.E.P.O. so that a crew which spreads out through a level still knows who is where and what is happening.
version: R.E.P.O. 0.4.0, as installed for this build (see the sources page for the exact version string)
prerequisites: A level with more than one room in it
A crew that is willing to say where they are

steps.do: Carry the walkie-talkie rather than assuming you can always talk: it is an item you equip, not something the player has built in.
steps.because: the walkie-talkie is a carried item with a light and materials of its own (itemEquippable, itemLight, NormalMaterial, BlackMaterial)

steps.do: Watch the device itself for who is on the channel, because it keeps a record of who is holding it and which sets are in use.
steps.because: it keeps a record of who is on it and which sets are being used (inThisWalkie, someoneInThisWalkie, walkiesBeingUsed, otherWalkie)

steps.do: Read its lines and its eyes when you are trying to reach someone, since the walkie shows its state rather than only making a noise.
steps.because: it shows its state with two lines, a scrolling texture and eyes of its own (lineRendererL, lineRendererR, lineTextureScrollSpeed, mshRenderersEyes)

steps.do: Tune and wire deliberately: tuning in, tuning out, wiring in and wiring out are four separate actions with a sound each.
steps.because: it carries tuning and wiring sounds of its own (tuneInSound, tuneOutSound, wireInSound, wireOutSound)

steps.do: Treat interference as information rather than a fault, because the walkie keeps interference loops and a breaker for them.
steps.because: it carries interference loops and a breaker for the interference (interferenceLoop, interferenceInsideLoop, interferenceBreaker)

steps.do: Do not expect to type while a job has you locked, because some of them lock the chat box.
steps.because: starting the truck and clearing slackers lock the chat box (LockedStartingTruck, LockedDestroySlackers)

steps.do: Send a message and then watch it move, because a message has states of its own between being written and being sent.
steps.because: a message moves through states of its own (ChatState, Inactive, Active, Possessed, Send)

steps.do: Use the lobby chat before the run and the crew chat during it, because they are two different interfaces.
steps.because: the lobby and the run have separate chat interfaces (LobbyChatUI, ChatUI)

steps.do: Read the map for the crew and for the monsters rather than only for the valuables, because each has a marker of its own.
steps.because: monsters and the player each have their own marker on the map (DirtFinderMapEnemy, DirtFinderMapPlayer)

steps.do: Expect the map to fill in as you go rather than being complete when you arrive, because it backtracks and scans.
steps.because: the map is drawn in layers and fills in over time (MapLayer, MapBacktrack, DirtFinderMapScanlines)

commonMistakes: Leaving the walkie-talkie in the truck and finding out when the level splits the crew.
Assuming a silent walkie means nobody is talking, when the interference and the session state are shown on the device.
Trying to type while a job has the chat box locked.
Treating the map as a full picture of the level rather than one that fills in as you move.
sources: This installation of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
